description:
A default password opened doors it never should have. A trusted update delivered malware. Even a security feature became a way to break in. Different stories, same problem: the things meant to protect us aren't always doing their job.

Meanwhile, AI is making bug hunting faster, old flaws are still paying off, and attackers keep finding easy ways in. Some attacks take real skill. Others barely
title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: N-able 0-Days, Windows 0-Days, Chrome 0-Days, Fridge 0-Days, and More Bad Days

description:
Google on Monday revealed that adversarial use of artificial intelligence (AI) by threat actors has gone beyond manual prompting to deploying autonomous multi-agent offensive frameworks like ARTEX, CAIRN, CyberStrikeAI, and PentAGI to execute multi-stage intrusions at greater operational velocity.

In tandem, threat actors are leveraging the power and capabilities of large language models (LLMs)
title: Google Finds Hackers Using AI Agents to Build and Run Exploits From Software Patches

title: Retadup Worm Resurfaces 7 Years After Takedown to Spread CoffeeLoader Malware

description:
Six flaws in Danfoss AK-SM800A refrigeration controllers could let a remote attacker take over a controller without logging in, Dutch security consultancy Midnight Blue said earlier this week.

No patch is available, and the researchers say the newest firmware, version 5.4.0, does not fix the flaws.

title: Six Unpatched Danfoss Refrigeration Controller Flaws Could Allow Remote Takeover Without Login

title: SANSAR Linux Cryptomining Malware Uses Modified NVIDIA Library to Hide GPU Activity

description:

title: BO Team Exploits Log4Shell in VMware vCenter, Compromises Russian Firm's Code-Signing Server

description:
Attackers' AI agents have been hunting for weak spots in internet-exposed AI apps such as LiteLLM, One API, and Dify to steal the AI provider keys stored inside, according to the agents' own records.

The records, which Amazon's threat intelligence team captured with decoy servers, describe stolen keys being used to run the AI models that powered the search for more keys.

title: Amazon Uncovers AI Agent Campaign Targeting LiteLLM, Dify, and Other Apps for API Keys
